episodes.title: Bots Behaving Badly + Is AI Regulation On The Right Track + Kevin’s Sloppelganger
episodes.about: On the first episode of Machine Gods, Kevin Roose and Casey Newton ask: How worried should we be about rogue AI agents? After OpenAI's Hugging Face breach, we discuss the first sighting of a rogue AI agent fleet linked to a Chinese AI company, Anthropic's Claude sending a bogus homicide tip to Philadelphia police, and a new Anthropic report warning AI agents may be months away from self-replicating on smart TVs and other home devices. Then, who's going to rein this in? We size up President Trump's new Super Intelligence Force, the FTC subpoenas and EU AI Act investigations into OpenAI and Anthropic, and ask whether regulators are anywhere close to getting this right. And finally, Kevin investigates his sloppelganger: someone made an AI-generated rip-off of his new book, The AGI Chronicles, and sold it on Amazon.
episodes.why: The first full episode of Roose and Newton's new show: rogue agent fleets, the Hugging Face breach, Claude's bogus homicide tip, and whether Trump's Super Intelligence Force and the FTC can rein any of it in.

episodes.title: The New Apex Predator: CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz on Adversaries Armed With AI Agents
episodes.about: Adversaries are already running AI agents, and the fastest attacks now play out in seconds. Sarah Guo and Elad Gil sit down with CrowdStrike president and CEO George Kurtz on what AI-equipped attackers mean for enterprise security. George explains how agents are flattening the adversary pyramid by putting advanced tradecraft in the hands of low-skill attackers, and why CrowdStrike and Nvidia are building a frontier-style lab of their own to train security models. They also get into how open-weight and closed models compare on security, where CrowdStrike is directing its platform investment, lessons from the recent Hugging Face incident, and why George sees AI, like every platform shift before it, as a net creator of opportunity.
episodes.why: Out today: CrowdStrike's George Kurtz on attackers running AI agents at inference speed, the flattened adversary pyramid, and the frontier security lab CrowdStrike is building with Nvidia.

episodes.title: How AI Is Changing What Work Means
episodes.about: Why is a financial research firm using AI to design proteins that target scorpion venom? Because AI is changing what work means - and what businesses are capable of doing. Citrini Research's unexpected experiment opens up bigger questions about who gets to do science, whether AI labs will compete with their customers, and how far companies can push beyond their traditional expertise. In the headlines: Muse hits 10 million US downloads, Gemini gets more personal in Android Auto, and Anthropic's financial disclosures spark fresh valuation debates.
episodes.why: A finance firm is designing anti-venom proteins with AI: NLW on who gets to do science now and labs competing with their own customers, plus Muse at 10M downloads and Anthropic's valuation debate.

episodes.title: Bill Gates says to prepare for 20 years of ‘tumultuous’ AI disruption
episodes.about: My guest today is Bill Gates, co-founder and former CEO of Microsoft and chairman of the Gates Foundation. You may have noticed Bill in the news more lately - he's been on something of a tour for the past few months talking about AI risk, and how crucial it is that we start taking this seriously. So I was excited to sit down with him and really dig into this subject. I came with many questions, about AI policy, the technical aspects of alignment, and what it means for future generations that we're building something this disruptive and potentially dangerous.
episodes.why: Out today: Gates is on an AI-risk tour and sits down with Nilay Patel for the long version - policy, alignment, and what 20 years of disruption means for the next generation.

episodes.title: Christina Cacioppo - Building an Enduring Software Company in the Age of AI
episodes.about: My guest today is Christina Cacioppo, founder and CEO of Vanta, which helps more than 16,000 companies manage security and compliance. Five years after our first conversation, we discuss how Vanta became a category leader, what it takes to reinvent a successful software business in the age of AI, and why Christina is betting on agents to do the work rather than simply assist users. We also explore the changing economics of software, the war for exceptional talent, AI's impact on cybersecurity, and what it takes to build an enduring company in Silicon Valley's rapidly changing environment.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Colossus's investor interview show, new to the list: Vanta CEO Christina Cacioppo on rebuilding a 16,000-customer compliance company agent-first, eating the cost of AI, and outcome pricing.
